summary: Weekly POC sync focused on increasing effective throughput. topics: Continuous batching and prefix caching impacts
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Ok good morning everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check, audio okay?
[00:05] Laura: yep, sounds good.
[00:08] Maya: Cool. Today we'll run through the bench results from last night, then daniel will walk through a proposed tuning for batching and concurrency, and we'll decide the next overnight run.
[00:20] Daniel: hey all, so we re-ran the 50k sample with the new continuous batching flags enabled, we saw avg throughput increase about 18%, p50 dropped a little but p95 moved up slightly when concurrency hit 24.
[00:35] Priya: can you repeat the numbers, p95 went up when you increased concurrency? that seems counterintuitive.
[00:40] Daniel: yeah so short story, when you crank concurrency the runtime batches more aggressively but you start seeing queueing inside the worker for long sequences, that increases tail. average token throughput improves but tail suffers unless we cap per-request concurrency or enable backpressure.
[00:54] Arjun: what's the actual p95 and p99 we're seeing? we need numbers for SRE.
[00:58] Daniel: p50 about 120ms, p95 ~420ms, p99 ~950ms on the last run with concurrency 24 and continuous batching on default thresholds. throughput steady at ~820 reqs/min.
[01:12] Maya: for context NovaPay's target is 5k QPS for peak flows, but realistic steady 800-1200 rps during daytime windows, with 200ms p95 goal for UI flows.
[01:25] Laura: yes 200ms p95 for our customer-facing UI calls, background jobs can be slower.
[01:30] Priya: our samples have 70% short requests (<128 tokens) and 30% long (>512 tokens), so the variance is large.
[01:40] Daniel: that's important, continuous batching benefits the short tail but long sequences hold KV cache and block execution path. we recommended a mixed strategy: set concurrency target to 12 for UI endpoints and 24 for batch endpoints, plus enable prefix KV caching for the short requests to reduce repeated compute.
[01:58] Arjun: how does KV cache help in throughput? we weren't sure if that would increase memory pressure on the GPUs.
[02:03] Daniel: correct, it uses more GPU memory but reduces per-request token compute because prefix tokens don't get recomputed. memory impact depends on window size; we suggested a 4k token window for this workload which fits on your A100 80GB nodes in the dedicated test fleet.
[02:18] Priya: wait our hardware for POC is mixed, some runs use 80GB A100s, some on 48GB VMs in the cloud. is the recommendation different?
[02:26] Daniel: yeah we profiled both — on 48GB we recommend a smaller cache window (1k) and lower concurrency target to avoid OOM and GPU thrashing, you'll get smaller batching benefits but still net throughput wins.
[02:36] Maya: also need to consider queuing/backpressure at the ingress—if client retries on 429s it can create cascading load. we advised adding a little jitter and retry-after hints.
[02:48] Laura: I flagged that with our client teams; they have aggressive retries in some mobile clients. we can throttle them at the gateway but we need guidance on safe queue lengths.
[02:56] Daniel: empirically we found safe queue depth per worker around 64 requests for your short-request mix with concurrency 12; above that tail starts to move. for long-request heavy workers safe queue is closer to 16.
[03:10] Priya: could we get a simple matrix from you mapping concurrency, queue depth, and expected p95 for the two hardware profiles? that would help our SREs tune autoscaling.
[03:18] Maya: yes that's in the action items — we'll send a concurrency/batching matrix and cost delta estimates.
[03:24] Daniel: quick note on batching thresholds — we saw that lowering the wait window from 20ms to 8ms hurt throughput on short bursts, but improved p95 because batches formed faster but smaller. So there's a tradeoff.
[03:36] Arjun: so what should we tune first? lower wait window or cap concurrency?
[03:40] Daniel: cap concurrency for UI flows first to meet the 200ms p95. then tweak wait window if you still need more throughput without hurting tail.
[03:48] Laura: any changes needed on our SDK side?
[03:51] Daniel: minimal—add the prefer-low-latency header for UI calls so the router favors instances with lower queue depth, and implement exponential backoff with jitter on 429s. Also send the sequence-length hint in the request metadata so the router can shard appropriately.
[04:06] Priya: we can add length hint. but I'm worried about inaccurate hints if mobile clients don't send them.
[04:12] Maya: that's fine — router will fall back to conservative defaults if no hint. it's best-effort.
[04:18] Daniel: on cost, moving from concurrency 24->12 reduces GPU utilization slightly, roughly 12% increase in cost per successful request if you need to maintain raw throughput, but for UI use we'll accept that for better latency. We'll include exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:33] Laura: did you try the newer quantized kernel set? last week you mentioned a 4-bit run that looked promising.
[04:38] Daniel: yes, quantized run reduced memory and increased batch sizes, but introduced small quality regressions on some prompts. For background jobs it's fine; for UI we need to run evals first. We'll annotate which endpoints are safe to use quantized variants.
[04:51] Arjun: regarding autoscaling, if we cap concurrency and have variable load, what's the safe panic scale threshold? we don't want to overshoot and incur cost.
[04:59] Daniel: typical policy: scale up when avg queue depth across pool > 50 for 2 consecutive minutes; scale down when < 20 for 10 minutes. We'll provide numbers tuned to your traffic pattern.
[05:09] Priya: ok good. about the overnight run, what's the dataset and parameters?
[05:13] Maya: NovaPay will run the 10k mixed-length synthetic trace with concurrency matrix [6,12,18,24] across both HW profiles, continuous batching flags on, and the wait-window set to default 20ms. Also run a variant with wait-window 8ms. Share logs and perf csv.
[05:27] Laura: will do. we'll kick it off at 0200 and should have results by tomorrow morning.
[05:31] Daniel: also please include the token distribution and response size histogram, that helps explain p99 spikes.
[05:37] Priya: noted.
[05:39] Maya: ok let's recap next steps. daniel you'll prepare the matrix and the per-profile recommended configs, maya will add cost deltas and a notes doc, novaPay will run overnight test and share results, and we schedule the deep dive on queueing with your infra team next week.
[05:55] Laura: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[05:58] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and link to the logs. bye.
[06:03] [call end]
notes: Transcript has intermittent speaker attribution inconsistencies (Daniel sometimes labelled as Speaker 2 in the raw capture). Bench numbers approximate from last-night run. References: perf spreadsheet link (shared in chat), config snippets, and eval report to follow.
